title: Presidential Message on National Forest Products Week
body: Briefings & Statements Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research From the misty evergreens of the Pacific Northwest to the hardwood ridges of Appalachia, America’s forests are among our Nation’s greatest natural treasures. During National Forest Products Week, we renew our commitment to conserving these incredible landscapes and responsibly harnessing their abundance to sustain households, strengthen American jobs and industry, and secure lasting prosperity for generations to come. The woodlands of America helped build our Nation from the ground up, giving generations of citizens the resources to raise homes, establish businesses, and pursue their dreams. That proud tradition continues today in our logging, forestry, manufacturing, and construction industries, where the bounty of our land meets the skill and resolve of our people in communities across our country. As President, I am committed to supporting these vital industries and continuing to drive economic growth. Last year, I was proud to sign two Executive Orders to increase domestic timber supply and reduce reliance on imports from foreign markets. As a result, over half a billion dollars in new domestic industry investments were announced and the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Forest Service has sold over three billion board feet of American timber this year, the highest volume sold in almost three decades. Under my leadership, the USDA Forest Service has also championed sustainable forests, achieving 116 percent of our annual reforestation goal, the highest level in twenty-six years. We are cutting red tape and rolling back unnecessary environmental regulations on industries such as logging and paper manufacturing, unleashing the full productive power of American workers and natural resources. I also established the Make America Beautiful Again Commission, which brings together members of my Administration to lead active forest management and historic conservation efforts that will preserve the magnificent abundance of our wildlands for the Americans who will inherit them in the centuries ahead. This week, we reflect on God’s gift of our beautiful and immense natural landscape, and we refocus our efforts to responsibly and boldly utilize these resources to grow our Republic, strengthen our economy, and empower American families with the tools and opportunities they need to build our Nation’s future. body: Briefings & Statements Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research On Tuesday, October 20, 2026, the President signed into law: H.R. 227, the “Clergy Act,” which allows a 2-year period in which ministers of a church, members of a religious order, and Christian Science practitioners may submit an application to the Internal Revenue Service to revoke their exemption from Social Security coverage; H.R. 837, which requires the Secretary of Agriculture to convey the Pleasant Valley Ranger District Administrative Site, located on the Tonto National Forest, to Gila County, Arizona; H.R. 1721, the “Critical Infrastructure Manufacturing Feasibility Act,” which requires the Department of Commerce to conduct a study on the costs, benefits, and feasibility of manufacturing any high-demand product in the United States that is being imported due to a manufacturing, material, or supply chain constraint; H.R. 2388, the “Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe Project Lands Restoration Act,” which takes certain land in the State of Washington into trust for the benefit of the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe; H.R. 2481, the “Romance Scam Prevention Act,” which requires online dating service providers to provide to a member of the online dating service a fraud ban notification if the member has received a message through the service from a member who was banned due to fraudulent activity; H.R. 3620, the “Southcentral Foundation Land Transfer Act of 2025,” which requires the warranty deed conveyance of land in Anchorage, Alaska, to the Southcentral Foundation; H.R. 4307, the “Enhancing Detection of Human Trafficking Act,” which requires the Secretary of Labor to provide training to certain employees of the Department of Labor on how to detect and assist law enforcement in preventing human trafficking during the course of their official duties; H.R. 4467, the “Vicksburg National Military Park Boundary Modification Act,” which directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey approximately seven acres of Federal land, located within the boundaries of the Vicksburg National Military Park, to the State of Mississippi for construction of a new interpretive center; H.R. 6380, the “Chiricahua National Park Act,” which redesignates the Chiricahua National Monument, located in southeastern Arizona, as the Chiricahua National Park; H.R. 7831, the “License to Drill Act,” which extends the authority of the Department of the Interior to collect certain oil and gas permit application processing fees. body: USTR Announces 2026 Award Recipients pbrouillette Wed, 10/21/2026 - 19:05 WASHINGTON — Today, the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) hosted its annual awards ceremony, celebrating the achievements and notable milestones of its staff. During the program, award recipients were announced in the following categories: Ambassador’s Award, William B. Kelly Award, Linda Enoch Award, Excellence in Service Award, Erland Herfindahl Award, Superior Achievement Award, Distinguished Career Service Award, Team Award, Way to Go Award, and Length of Service Award. “Through their unwavering commitment to public service and pursuit of excellence, the USTR team has helped advance and execute President Trump’s America First Trade Policy, delivering lasting benefits for American farmers, manufacturers, workers, and businesses of all sizes,” said Ambassador Jamieson Greer . “Our team embodies the true meaning of public service, leading with integrity and professionalism. From our economists and legal counsel to our trade negotiators and overseas staff, I am very appreciative of your hard work and dedication to advance the agency’s mission.” USTR is pleased to announce the 2026 award recipients: Ambassador’s Award – Recognizes a senior USTR employee who demonstrates excellence, leadership, and tenacity, and whose contributions go significantly beyond the standard and requirements of their role: Daniel Watson, former Assistant United States Trade Representative for the Western Hemisphere William B. Kelly Award – Recognizes an employee who demonstrates the highest standard of professional excellence in the trade field and demonstrates sustained contributions and leadership in advancing USTR’s goals, an exemplary degree of initiative and creativity, and great respect from peers and superiors: Rebecca Gudicello, Deputy Assistant United States Trade Representative for Market Access and Industrial Competitiveness Linda Enoch Award – Recognizes dedicated service and excellence in administrative management, including the qualities of professionalism, initiative, creativity, and respect of peers: JoAnne Allen, Trade Research Specialist for Economics Excellence in Service Award – Recognizes an employee who has made an extraordinary contribution in an administrative services and mission support position: Calvin Jackson, Information Technology Specialist Erland Herfindahl Award – Recognizes an employee who exemplifies the values that strengthen the heart of our community – compassion, decency, empathy and kindness, and who contributes tangibly and consistently to the cohesion and vitality of our agency – not just through what they do, but through how they do it: Jennifer Oetken, Deputy Assistant United States Trade Representative for Labor Affairs Superior Achievement Award – Recognizes employees for special efforts significantly above and beyond the requirements for their position: Leslie Akinola, Daniel Arias, Victor Ban, Angela Brown, Celeste Chen, Cassie Ender, Elizabeth Falkner, Emily Fischer, Conor Harrington, Michelle Ker, Amy Kreps, Della Little, Amanda Mayhew, Colette Morgan, Sarah Morningred, Asad Nawaz, Michael Remetta, Zeba Reyazuddin, Leo Roytman, Sofia Ruiz, Deborah Tidwell, Margaret Wang, Benjamin Wollam, and Wallis Yu Distinguished Career Service Award – Recognizes recent USTR retiree(s) whose career reflects long and exceptional devotion to duty and exemplifies significant contributions to the economy, efficiency, uniquely important projects, recognized expertise in some phase of USTR’s technical, professional or administrative work or other improvement in USTR operation: Connie Hamilton, former Assistant title: Adjusting Imports of Wind Turbines and Their Parts and Components into the United States
body: Presidential Actions Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA A PROCLAMATION 1. Within the past 90 days, the Secretary of Commerce (Secretary) transmitted to me a report on his investigation into the effects of imports of wind turbines and their parts and components on the national security of the United States under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, as amended, 19 U.S.C. 1862 (section 232). Based on the facts considered in that investigation, and taking into account the close relation of the economic welfare of the Nation to our national security and other relevant factors, see section 232(d) (19 U.S.C. 1862(d)), the Secretary found and advised me of his opinion that wind turbines and their components and subcomponents are being imported into the United States under such circumstances as to threaten to impair the national security of the United States and provided me recommendations for action under section 232 to adjust the imports of wind turbines and their components and subcomponents so that such imports will not threaten to impair the national security of the United States. 2. Among other things, the Secretary found that wind energy is an unreliable and intermittent energy source and that the use of wind energy diverts the United States electrical grid from more reliable energy sources. And the Secretary found that imports of wind turbine components and subcomponents have increased over the last decade, and that United States wind energy is reliant on imports of foreign produced wind turbine components and subcomponents. 3. The Secretary found that wind energy is intermittent and burdensome on the United States electrical grid. This results in higher operational costs and increased maintenance burdens. 4. title: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Domestic Petroleum Production, Refining, and Logistics Capacity
body: Presidential Actions Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research MEMORANDUM FOR THE SECRETARY OF WAR SUBJECT: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Domestic Petroleum Production, Refining, and Logistics Capacity On January 20, 2025, I issued Executive Order 14156 (Declaring a National Energy Emergency), under the National Emergencies Act. That order found that America’s inadequate energy production, transportation, refining, and generation capacity constitute an unusual and extraordinary threat to the Nation’s economy, national security, and foreign policy. It emphasized that our Nation’s current inadequate and intermittent energy supply leaves us vulnerable to hostile foreign actors and poses an imminent and growing threat to the prosperity and national security of the United States. Consistent with that declaration, I find that ensuring resilient domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity is central to United States defense readiness. Petroleum fuels the Nation’s Armed Forces, industrial base, and crucial infrastructure. Without immediate Federal action, United States defense capabilities will remain vulnerable to disruption. Therefore, by the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including section 303 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended (the “Act”) (50 U.S.C. 4533), I hereby determine, pursuant to section 303(a)(5) of the Act, that: (1) domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity, including exploration and production, gathering and transmission pipelines, storage, and marine terminals, are industrial resources, materials, or critical technology items essential to the national defense; (2) without Presidential action under section 303 of the Act, United States industry cannot reasonably be expected to provide these capabilities for the needed industrial resource, material, or critical technology item in a timely manner due to constrained financing, long lead times, permitting and infrastructure bottlenecks, and supply chain limitations; and (3) purchases, purchase commitments, financial support for the development of production capabilities, or other action pursuant to section 303 of the Act are the most cost-effective, expedient, and practical alternative methods for meeting this need. I have declared a national emergency under Executive Order 14156, and I further determine that action to expand the domestic petroleum production, refining, and logistics capacity is necessary to avert an industrial resource or critical technology item shortfall that would severely impair national defense capability. Therefore, pursuant to section 303(a)(7) of the Act, I waive the requirements of section 303(a)(1)-(a)(6) of the Act for the purpose of expanding such capability. You are authorized and directed to implement this determination, including making necessary purchases, commitments, and financial instruments to enable these projects, and to publish this determination in the Federal Register . Any provision of previous memoranda, proclamations, and Executive Orders that is inconsistent with this determination is superseded to the extent of such inconsistency. DONALD J. Food security is national security — we recognize that our fisheries are a vital pillar of American independence. This National Seafood Month, I join the American people in celebrating these hardworking men and women and reaffirm my commitment to helping them compete, prosper, and lead the world in seafood production. From the fishing ports of early America to today’s seafood farms and processing plants, this great industry has rewarded enterprise, sustained family businesses, and helped forge the unmatched spirit of determination that defines our maritime workforce. For generations, our fishermen have braved rough seas and punishing storms, spending long days far from home to earn an honest living and provide for the people they love. Across our land, the incredible American seafood industry harvests nearly 8.5 billion pounds of world-class food annually, sustains more than a million jobs, and fuels more than $173 billion in commerce, bringing wealth and opportunity to communities across our great Nation. And now, as we usher in a new Golden Age of seafood production, we are ensuring our fishing communities remain places where the next generation can raise a family, build a business, and pursue their own share of the American Dream. Since returning to office, I have taken decisive action to restore American seafood competitiveness and give our fishing communities greater freedom to grow and succeed. Last year, I signed an Executive Order to restore American seafood competitiveness, and my Administration recently launched the Department of Agriculture Office of Seafood. I have also signed three proclamations to restore commercial fishing access to nearly 5,000 square miles in the Atlantic Ocean and to hundreds of thousands of square miles in the Pacific, enabling American vessels to work additional fishing grounds and compete more effectively in the global seafood market. Under my leadership, we delivered the largest single-year quota increase in the history of the United States Atlantic bluefin tuna fishery, secured a massive 1,200 percent quota increase for Atlantic mackerel, and revived the West Coast salmon season to yield the first full commercial fishery in 3 years. My Administration was also proud to allocate $123.6 million in fishery disaster assistance to help communities recover from devastating losses, strengthen shoreside infrastructure, and support job retraining to help workers get back on their feet. We will continue slashing burdensome regulations so our fishermen can reinvest in their fleets, expand their operations, and keep more of what they earn. Through these historic efforts, we are putting American fishermen first and fighting to make our Nation the strongest, most successful seafood producer in the world. As our Nation celebrates National Seafood Month, we give thanks to the families whose skill and sacrifice have built and sustained this essential American industry for over 250 years. We will stand with them as we build a future of thriving ports, successful businesses, and an American seafood industry that is stronger, more competitive, and more prosperous than ever before. title: United States and Mexico Announce Course of Remediation at Minera Peñasquito
body: United States and Mexico Announce Course of Remediation at Minera Peñasquito pbrouillette Fri, 10/23/2026 - 09:06 WASHINGTON — The Office of the United States Trade Representative and the Government of Mexico (Mexico) today announced a course of remediation at Minera Peñasquito, S.A. de C.V. (Newmont Peñasquito), located in the state of Zacatecas, Mexico. The remediation plan will help ensure workers at the facility can freely exercise their right to freedom of association and collective bargaining. Actions already taken by the company to address the matter include: Posting and dissemination of a neutrality statement and company guidelines on freedom of association and collective bargaining; and Installation of a complaint mechanism for workers to report violations of their rights anonymously and confidentially. Under the course of remediation, Mexico will ensure that Newmont Peñasquito will, among other things: Reinstate and provide full backpay and benefits to two workers; Distribute hard copies of the neutrality statement and company guidelines related to freedom of association and collective bargaining to all company personnel; Implement the neutrality statement and company guidelines on freedom of association and collective bargaining, including a zero-tolerance policy for violations; Publicly acknowledge, through meetings with the workers and postings at the facility, the company’s unlawful and interfering practices; Conduct in-person training for all company personnel during work hours regarding rights related to freedom of association and collective bargaining; and Maintain its complaint mechanism for workers to report violations of their rights anonymously and confidentially. Under the course of remediation, Mexico will: Review and facilitate the reinstatement and severance processes to ensure two workers receive reinstatement offers and full backpay and benefits, or full severance payments, as applicable; and Maintain a direct email address and telephone line for workers to anonymously report any potential acts of unlawful interference or other violations of workers’ freedom of association and collective bargaining rights. The United States and Mexico agreed to establish a deadline of October 28, 2026 to complete the course of remediation. Background The United States Trade Representative and the Secretary of Labor co-chair the Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement (ILC). On May 13, 2026, the ILC received an RRM petition from the Sindicato Nacional de Trabajadores Mineros, Metalúrgicos, Siderúrgicos y Similares de la República Mexicana (Los Mineros) , a Mexican labor union. The petition alleged that Newmont Peñasquito had violated workers’ rights by retaliating against workers for engaging in union activity, including through unlawful dismissals. The ILC reviews RRM petitions that it receives, and the accompanying information, within 30 days. The ILC determined that there was sufficient, credible evidence of a denial of rights enabling the good faith invocation of enforcement mechanisms. As a result, the United States Trade Representative submitted a request that Mexico review whether workers at Newmont Peñasquito were being denied the right to freedom of association and collective bargaining. Mexico agreed to conduct a review. Following Mexico’s investigation, the United States and Mexico agreed on a course of remediation. Read the full course of remediat ion here . Read an unofficial courtesy Spanish translation of the full course of remediation here . ###

title: First Lady Melania Trump Secures Ceasefire Between Russia and Ukraine, Localized to Oleshky
body: Office of the First Lady Briefings & Statements Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research First Lady Melania Trump successfully secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, localized to the city of Oleshky. Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway. The localized ceasefire will begin on October 29, 2026. “The situation in Oleshky is dire. Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster. Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water,” said First Lady Melania Trump. “The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks. It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible.” First Lady Melania Trump and her representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the localized ceasefire. The First Lady initiated discussions with both nations and aligned the parties on the agreement’s objectives, technical procedures, timing, processes, and terms, in her formal role as Exclusive Intermediary. “Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require. Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” said First Lady Melania Trump. The First Lady continued, “I have also secured an impartial American media organization to accompany and document Russian and Ukrainian teams on the ground throughout the process. This will play a significant role in ensuring that the wishes of each family are faithfully respected.” The exigent circumstances of Oleshky came to First Lady Melania Trump’s attention during a private discussion at her Fostering the Future Together event in New York City during the 81st United Nations General Assembly. “My representative and I immediately leveraged the communication channel we established with Russia and Ukraine through the previous six reunifications of 34 children. Both nations promptly assigned teams to coordinate the complex mechanics involved, including demining. All parties have worked around the clock since that moment,” explained First Lady Melania Trump. All media inquiries for the Office of the First Lady should be directed to OFLPress@who.eop.gov . About Oleshky Oleshky is located in southern Ukraine, directly across from the Dnipro River in Kherson. Before the war, roughly 24,000 people lived in Oleshky. Today, an estimated 1700-2000 residents remain, primarily older people who have been unable to leave, along with approximately 50 children. There has not been a formal demographic count in Oleshky since 2022. Since the war began, the city has remained on the front line, with much of its population displaced or evacuated. Following the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam, approximately 90 percent of the city’s territory was flooded. The post First Lady Melania Trump Secures Ceasefire Between Russia and Ukraine, Localized to Oleshky appeared first on The White House .

title: FURTHER MODIFYING THE SCOPE OF PRODUCTS OF CANADA SUBJECT TO THE ADDITIONAL DUTIES IMPOSED TO OFFSET CANADIAN DISCRIMINATION AGAINST THE COMMERCE OF THE UNITED STATES WITH RESPECT TO MOTOR VEHICLES
body: Presidential Actions Search Select Category All News Briefings & Statements All Presidential Actions Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research All Briefings & Statements Presidential Actions All Executive Orders Nominations & Appointments Presidential Memoranda Proclamations Fact Sheets Releases Remarks Research BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA A PROCLAMATION 1. In Proclamation 11048 of July 20, 2026 (Imposing Additional Duties To Offset Canadian Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect to Motor Vehicles), I found as a fact that Canada is discriminating in fact against the commerce of the United States through Canada’s motor vehicle tariff scheme; that this discrimination places the commerce of the United States at a disadvantage compared to the commerce of other countries; and that Canada’s imposition is unreasonable, is not equally enforced upon the like articles of every foreign country, and places a burden on the commerce of the United States. To offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce from Canada’s discrimination or unreasonable and unequal imposition on U.S. auto and auto parts exports, I imposed under section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1338) (section 338) additional ad valorem duties, effective August 19, 2026, on certain products of Canada. 2. In Proclamation 11056 of August 18, 2026 (Temporary Suspension of Additional Duties To Offset Canadian Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect to Alcoholic Beverages, Dairy, and Motor Vehicles), I temporarily suspended for 3 days the effective date of the additional ad valorem duties imposed under Proclamation 11048 after Canada expressed a commitment to remove the discrimination or unreasonable and unequal imposition at issue in Proclamation 11048. 3. On August 21, 2026, Canada reneged on its commitment, ceased negotiating in good faith, and did not remove the discrimination or unreasonable and unequal imposition at issue in Proclamation 11048. 4. Accordingly, at 12:01 a.m. eastern time on August 22, 2026, the 3-day suspension imposed by Proclamation 11056 lapsed, and the additional ad valorem duties imposed under Proclamation 11048 became effective. 5. In Proclamation 11065 of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope of Products of Canada Subject to the Additional Duties Imposed To Offset Canadian Discrimination Against the Commerce of the United States With Respect to Motor Vehicles), I modified the duties imposed under Proclamation 11048 after receiving certain information, opinions, and recommendations from senior executive branch officials to continue offsetting the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce and better serve the public interest. 6. I have received certain additional information, opinions, and recommendations from senior executive branch officials on the status of the circumstances involved in Proclamation 11048 and the effect of the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, including how effectively those duties are offsetting the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce. According to senior executive branch officials, although the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce, modifying the scope of products subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, would still offset the burden or disadvantage on U.S. commerce and better serve the public interest. In my senior executive branch officials’ opinion, modifying the scope of products subject to the additional ad valorem duties imposed in Proclamation 11048, as amended, is required by the public interests and is consistent with the interests of the United States. 7. title: United States Announces Successful Resolution of Rapid Response Labor Mechanism Matter at Amphenol Optimize
body: United States Announces Successful Resolution of Rapid Response Labor Mechanism Matter at Amphenol Optimize pbrouillette Fri, 10/23/2026 - 16:06 WASHINGTON — The United States today announced the successful resolution of the USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism (RRM) matter at the Amphenol Optimize México, S.A. de C.V. (Amphenol) facility located in Nogales, Sonora, Mexico, which manufactures automotive and aerospace connectors, cables, and components. The United States and Mexico agreed on a course of remediation to address labor rights violations occurring at the facility, including employer interference in union activity and retaliatory dismissals of workers. That plan has now been implemented, and the Denial of Rights concerns raised in the U.S. request for review have been remediated. As a result, the United States Trade Representative has directed the Secretary of the Treasury to resume liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the facility. Actions taken by the facility to address the matter include: Reinstating nine workers with full backpay and benefits; Implementing a neutrality statement and guidelines related to the freedom of association and collective bargaining; and Installing and publicizing a complaint mechanism through which workers can report violations of their rights and breaches of company policies. Actions taken by the Government of Mexico to address the matter include: Delivering in-person trainings for all company personnel on the freedom of association and collective bargaining; Monitoring the facility and engaging with workers and the company throughout its review period; and Maintaining a direct email address, reporting platform, and telephone line for workers to anonymously report any potential acts of unlawful interference or other violations of freedom of association and collective bargaining rights, and timely investigating any allegations. Background The United States Trade Representative and the Secretary of Labor co-chair the Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement (ILC). On April 11, 2025, the ILC received an RRM petition from the Sindicato Industrial Operaciones y Manufacturas , a Mexican labor union. The petition alleged that Amphenol had violated workers’ right to freedom of association and collective bargaining by coercing workers to vote for the company-favored outcome during a union vote, discouraging workers from joining an independent union, and taking reprisals against workers due to their union preferences, including through dismissals. The ILC reviews RRM petitions that it receives, and the accompanying information, within 30 days. The ILC determined that there was sufficient, credible evidence of a denial of rights enabling the good faith invocation of enforcement mechanisms. As a result, on May 9, 2025, the United States Trade Representative submitted a request to Mexico to review the matter. Mexico accepted the request, conducted an investigation, and worked with Amphenol to provide remediation to dismissed workers and implement facility-wide measures aimed at safeguarding freedom of association and collective bargaining rights. The United States has reviewed the matter and concluded the situation to have been remediated. As a result of the above actions taken by the facility and Mexico to resolve the action, the United States agrees that there is no ongoing denial of rights. Ambassador Greer’s letter directing the Secretary of the Treasury to resume liquidation of unliquidated entries of goods from the facility is available here . Read the full course of remediation here . Read an unofficial courtesy Spanish translation of the full course of remediation here . Information about previous requests can be found here . ###

Trump will open the South Lawn of the White House to trick or treaters of all ages. During this special White House tradition, thousands of children and their parents will proceed around the South Lawn to visit various trick-or-treat booths and enjoy spooky decorations featuring the harvest Moon on the South Portico of the White House. The event will take place from 3:30 PM to 7:00 PM and is open to ticketholders, including military families, law enforcement families, foster and adoptive families, and Administration officials with children. The President and First Lady will hand out commemorative candies on the South Drive for a portion of the event. Adding to the festivities and fun, the United States (U.S.) Air Force Strolling Strings will play traditional Halloween songs and modern tunes while the President and First Lady welcome children and families. Throughout the evening, the U.S. Postal Service will provide toy mail trucks and facilitate a BE BEST post card station for children. The U.S. Department of Agriculture will have a giant pumpkin photo opportunity and hand out mini pumpkins from American farmers. The U.S. Department of the Treasury will share coloring books as part of its promotion of Trump Accounts for young trick or treaters. The International Fresh Produce Association will provide apples from Michigan, and the National Confectioners Association will provide sweet treats to trick or treaters. The event will also feature participation and treats by America 250, National Aeronautics and Space Administration, National Park Service, U.S. Mint, U.S. Secret Service, and the Center of Science and Industry—which is providing a STEAM science-experiment kit for children. Please note that the U.S. Secret Service reserves the right to prohibit personal items, including but not limited to those mentioned at www.secretservice.gov/prohibiteditems . Strollers, wheelchairs, umbrellas (no metal tips), and cameras are permitted. All items needed for medical purposes will be permitted on the tour (such as wheelchairs, electric scooters, glucose tablets, and EpiPens). Please identify and explain all items needed for medical purposes to Secret Service agents upon arrival. This event will not be rescheduled if canceled due to inclement weather or any other reason. Attendees may call the 24-hour information line at (202) 456-7040 to check on the status of the event. The post First Lady Melania Trump Announces Halloween at the White House 2026 appeared first on The White House .

title: Ambassador Greer Issues Statement on the Status of the U.S.-EU Détente Following Record-Breaking Loan from the European Investment Bank to Airbus
body: Ambassador Greer Issues Statement on the Status of the U.S.-EU Détente Following Record-Breaking Loan from the European Investment Bank to Airbus pbrouillette Mon, 10/26/2026 - 18:59 WASHINGTON — Today, Ambassador Jamieson Greer issued a statement regarding the status of the U.S.-EU deal to pause duties on certain EU imports, following a record-breaking loan from the European Investment Bank to Airbus. “I had sincerely hoped that trade-distorting European subsidies to Airbus were a thing of the past,” said Ambassador Greer . “For decades, France, Germany, and Spain have aggressively supported Airbus, their national champion aircraft manufacturer, to gain an unfair advantage over U.S. aerospace workers and businesses. After winning at the WTO and imposing significant U.S. duties on EU imports in response, USTR struck a deal with the EU to pause those duties in exchange for a mutual commitment to provide financing to large civil aircraft (LCA) producers on market terms. Yet, this summer, almost immediately after the EU extended this pause, the European Investment Bank awarded Airbus its largest loan ever to benefit Airbus projects in France, Germany, and Spain. Despite ongoing requests, USTR still has no details about this loan. This situation injects substantial uncertainty into transatlantic trade in the aerospace sector. It is important this situation is resolved as soon as possible to ensure market-driven production in the aerospace sector and to avoid violation of the terms of our hard-won LCA deal.” ###

title: JUDGE ASKS FOR NOTIFICATION AS PUBLIC GOLF COURSE PROJECT, IN WASHINGTON, D.C., IS BUILT. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR TO APPEAL THIS UNCONSTITUTIONAL REQUEST. We are closing the East Potomac Golf Cours
body: JUDGE ASKS FOR NOTIFICATION AS PUBLIC GOLF COURSE PROJECT, IN WASHINGTON, D.C., IS BUILT. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR TO APPEAL THIS UNCONSTITUTIONAL REQUEST. We are closing the East Potomac Golf Course Site as scheduled on November 15th in order to renovate and rebuild for Competitive (with other such projects!), Safety, Modernization, and Aesthetic reasons. We believe this Project is totally "as of right," and that the judge does not have the Constitutional Right to "ask for or receive notices," which are time-consuming, unnecessary, expensive, and unconstitutional. We will immediately appeal this decision. When completed, it is anticipated that this Course, which will be open to the Public, at a reduced rate for those living in Washington, D.C., will be one of the finest anywhere in the World! It will be fully capable of holding Major Events such as The U.S. Open, The PGA Championship, The Ryder Cup, and The Presidents Cup, which will bring Great Economic Benefits, Growth, and Prestige to Washington, D.C. and, indeed, the entire surrounding area. The Development of this World Championship Public Facility must begin, immediately, if it is to be completed in a timely and seasonal manner. To have to give advanced notices to a judge who has no expertise in Golf, Architecture, Landscaping, Construction, or anything else having to do with building such a World Class Project, is not fair, appropriate, or Constitutional. The soil, grass, sand bunkers, tees, fairways, greens, seawalls, small and nondescript buildings, and virtually every other element of the existing Course and grounds are far beyond their intended or expected life. In its current form, the Course is extremely dangerous to play, in that the narrow and nondescript fairways are far too close together, leading to a constant barrage of people being hit with wayward shots, and the echoing throughout the air of the word, "FORE!" The judge has absolutely no right to hold up this very important and beautiful Project. We are asking the D.C. Circuit Court for immediate remedy. Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP

title: America First Seafood Strategy Charts Course to Restoring U.S. Seafood Dominance
body: America First Seafood Strategy Charts Course to Restoring U.S. Seafood Dominance myarbrough Wed, 10/28/2026 - 09:39 WASHINGTON – In honor of National Seafood Month, the White House unveiled the historic America First Seafood Strategy , outlining a whole-of-government approach to revitalize the U.S. fishing industry by removing foreign trade barriers and unlocking new markets for U.S. fishermen. Under President Trump’s leadership, U.S. seafood exports reached $5.53 billion in 2025, increasing 12% compared to 2024, and many of our trading partners have committed to remove trade barriers that undercut our global competitiveness. U.S. seafood exports are continuing to trend upwards in 2026. REELING IN THE WINS: The Trump Administration continues to secure new and enforce existing commitments from key trading partners to combat illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing, prevent forced labor on the high seas, and address harmful fisheries subsidies and other practices that distort markets and decimate the U.S. seafood industry. Taiwan committed to ensure that its fisheries subsidies do not contribute to overcapacity and overfishing and address violations of internationally recognized labor rights on board commercial fishing vessels. Read the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with Taiwan here . Argentina, Bangladesh, Ecuador, and Indonesia committed to combat IUU fishing, deter trade in IUU fishing-derived products, and address harmful fisheries subsidies through the use of robust fisheries management regimes. Read the Agreements on Reciprocal Trade with those countries here . USTR continues to engage and closely monitor Mexico’s implementation of its United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) fisheries-related environmental obligations, including its commitments to prevent illegal fishing in the Upper Gulf of California. FOREIGN TRADE PRACTICES PUT AMERICAN FISHERMEN ON THE HOOK: The United States is a global leader in responsibly managed fisheries and sustainable seafood — U.S. fisheries are scientifically monitored and legally enforced under 10 national standards of sustainability. Illegally caught and heavily subsidized foreign seafood, including seafood caught using forced labor on fishing vessels, are undercutting American fishermen that play by the rules. Every year, global losses from IUU fishing reach an estimated $50 billion with U.S. industry absorbing a major portion of that financial burden. In the America First Seafood Strategy, USTR spotlighted foreign trade barriers and distortive subsidies that continue to limit opportunities for U.S. seafood producers in key export markets. Japan imposes tariffs of up to 10% and enforces import quotas that disadvantage American exporters relative to competitors that benefit from preferential market access. The EU CATCH scheme imposes burdensome documentation and reporting requirements on U.S. fishermen despite the United States’ strong fisheries management and enforcement regime and safeguards against IUU fishing. India’s substantial fisheries subsidy program and Vietnam’s IUU fishing practices directly impact U.S. fishermen and supply chains, exporting seafood to the United States at lower-than-market prices. PUTTING AMERICAN FISHERMEN FIRST: President Trump’s trade policies will continue to expand market access for the 8.4 billion pounds of U.S. caught seafood each year and protect the 1.7 million jobs supported by America’s seafood industry. The future of seafood in the United States will be built by American fishermen, American workers, and American industry—not illegally-caught and heavily-subsidized foreign imports. In collaboration with other federal agencies, USTR will continue to use negotiations and enforcement tools to open new markets for U.S. exports and remove foreign trade that distort seafood trade and disadvantage U.S. fishermen. ###

Within the past 90 days, the Secretary of Commerce (Secretary) transmitted to me a report on his investigation into the effects of imports of robotics and industrial machinery, as well as their parts and components (together, components), on the national security of the United States under section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, as amended, 19 U.S.C. 1862 (section 232). Based on the facts considered in that investigation, and taking into account the close relation of the economic welfare of the Nation to our national security and other relevant factors, see section 232(d) (19 U.S.C. 1862(d)), the Secretary found and advised me of his opinion that robotics, industrial machinery, and their components are being imported into the United States in such quantities and under such circumstances as to threaten to impair the national security of the United States. 2. Nearly all modern defense systems and critical infrastructure sectors require the use of robotics or industrial machinery to function or be manufactured effectively and efficiently. Robotics and industrial machinery are critical to virtually all modern manufacturing processes, including for defense, commercial, and dual-use purposes. Robotics and industrial machinery enable defense readiness and design, production, and sustainment activities across a wide range of defense applications. Furthermore, robotics and industrial machinery generate substantial economic value and support important economic activities, including approximately $7.1 trillion in shipments of manufactured goods in 2024 and the production of approximately $86 billion worth of equipment in 2024. 3. The Secretary found that robotics and industrial machinery support the production of essential, state-of-the-art defense systems, such as aircraft, tanks, ships, weapons, and munitions, as well as certain military and law enforcement activities. For example, advanced robots — such as autonomous robots, humanoid and quadruped robots, and autonomous ground vehicles — provide combat support to the United States military, including by conducting intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions and by handling dangerous tasks, such as casualty extraction and mine detection and clearing. Robotics and industrial machinery also enable the defense industry to automate the building of essential defense products, such as missiles, aircraft, and ships, allowing production activities to last longer and for repetitive tasks to be performed with minimal error. Indeed, the defense industrial base’s ability to surge production, including during wartime or armed conflict, relies on industrial robotics and machinery. 4. The Secretary found that robotics and industrial machines are also crucial to the United States’ critical infrastructure sectors and other key aspects of the United States economy. Industrial robots and machines are used to create products and parts that are used across all 16 critical infrastructure sectors of the United States. For example, industrial robots are heavily used in the automotive, electrical, and electronics industries and are also meaningfully used in the metal and machinery, plastic and chemical products, and food and beverage industries. Similarly, industrial machinery carries out critical functions across various industries and in the manufacturing process for a range of goods, including construction equipment, electronics, medical devices, metal fabrication, motor vehicles, and aircraft.
